name: get_tables
description: Get a list of all tables, materialized views, views and live views in the QuestDB database

name: get_table_schema
description: Get the full schema definition (DDL) for a specific table, materialized view, view or live view

table_name.description: The name of the table, materialized view, view or live view to get schema for

name: get_table_details
description: Get the runtime details/statistics of a specific table, materialized view, view or live view

table_name.description: The name of the table, materialized view, view or live view to get details for

name: suggest_query
description: Suggest a SQL query to the user. The query will be displayed as a suggestion that the user can accept or reject. Always validate the query using validate_query before suggesting it.

query.description: The SQL query to suggest to the user

name: validate_query
description: Validate the syntax correctness of a SQL query using QuestDB's SQL syntax validator. All generated SQL queries should be validated using this tool before responding to the user.

name: get_questdb_toc
description: Get a table of contents listing all available QuestDB functions, operators, and SQL keywords. Use this first to see what documentation is available before requesting specific items.

name: get_questdb_documentation
description: Get documentation for specific QuestDB functions, operators, or SQL keywords. This is much more efficient than loading all documentation.

category.description: The category of documentation to retrieve

items.description: List of specific docs items in the category. IMPORTANT: Category of these items must match the category parameter. Name of these items should exactly match the entry in the table of contents you get with get_questdb_toc.

name: create_notebook
description: Create a new QuestDB notebook tab in the editor. You never see query data; this only scaffolds the tab and binds the current chat if it isn't already bound to a notebook. The tab is ALWAYS created in the background — you never switch the user's active tab. The user sees a notification and opens it themselves; only call activate_notebook if they explicitly ask to be taken there.

label.description: Label shown on the new notebook tab (max 100 characters). Pass null to use the default.

name: activate_notebook
description: Switch the user's editor to the given notebook tab so it becomes visible and focused. ONLY call this after the user has explicitly agreed to be taken to the notebook (e.g. they accepted your offer to open it). Never call it to auto-switch while the user is working elsewhere.

buffer_id.description: Notebook buffer id to activate (from a create_notebook result or the <notebook_context>/<workspace> prefix).

cell_to_focus.description: Optional cell id to focus and scroll into view after switching — useful to land the user on the specific cell you want them to see. Pass null to just open the tab without scrolling to a particular cell.

name: duplicate_notebook
description: Duplicate a notebook tab. Copies every cell (SQL, mode, chart config), layout, and run history into a NEW notebook labelled "<label> (copy)" placed right after the original; cell ids are regenerated. Matching saved result snapshots are copied best-effort in the background and hydrate when the copy is opened. `last_run_status` is preserved as history and does not guarantee that a saved result snapshot exists. The copy is ALWAYS made in the background — you never switch the user's active tab. The user sees a notification and opens it themselves; only call activate_notebook if they explicitly ask to be taken there.

name: delete_notebook
description: Archive (soft-delete) a notebook tab — the same as the user closing it with the X. It moves to history and the user can restore it; it is not permanently destroyed and query data is untouched. If this notebook is bound to the current chat, the binding goes stale (start a new one with create_notebook).

name: list_cells
description: List the cells in a notebook. Returns id, type, short preview (≤120 chars), position, mode, and last-run status. Mode is the presented result kind: `run` for a table result, `draw` for a chart, and null for editor-only/markdown cells. Three fields are LIVE-ONLY — present only while the notebook is open in the console, so absence never means "not refreshing" or "not blocked": `refreshing: true` while a refresh is in flight (the visible rows are still the previous round's), `last_refresh_error` when the last round left a failure, and `auto_refresh_blocked: "contains_write"` on cells auto-refresh will not run. `last_run_status` is unrelated to these: it stays the outcome of the last completed RUN, and a refresh never changes it. No cell data values.

name: get_cell
description: Get full details of a cell (value, kind via `type`, editor_height/result_height, view, chart config, last-run status + trimmed error). Height values are fixed CSS pixels or "auto". `view` reports what a SQL/draw cell presents: "editor" while there is nothing to show, else the stored result or editor_result arrangement. Markdown has no pane-view state: it reports `view` and `result_height` as null. Other LIVE-ONLY fields are `refreshing: true`, `last_refresh_error`, and `auto_refresh_blocked: "contains_write"`; absence never means "not refreshing" or "not blocked". `last_run_status` is unrelated to refresh state: it stays the outcome of the last completed RUN. `type:"markdown"` marks a prose cell whose `value` is markdown source; SQL cells omit `type`. Never includes query result data. By default the value is capped at 4 KB; a capped response carries `truncated: true` and `full_length`. A truncated value is NOT the cell's real content — NEVER write it back (update_cell / apply_notebook_state value); re-read with get_full_content: true first, or keep the cell with preserve_value: true.

get_full_content.description: True returns the verbatim full value with no cap (errors above 1 MB). Required before rewriting any cell whose read came back truncated. Null/omitted applies the 4 KB cap.

name: get_notebook_state
description: Full structural snapshot of a notebook (layout, cells with previews, semantic pane dimensions, kind via `type`, last-run statuses). Cell `grid` contains x/y/w only; height is derived from editor_height, result_height, and view. `view` reports what a SQL/draw cell presents: "editor" while there is nothing to show, else the stored result or editor_result arrangement. Markdown has no pane-view state: it reports `view` and `result_height` as null. Other LIVE-ONLY fields are `refreshing: true`, `last_refresh_error`, and `auto_refresh_blocked: "contains_write"`; absence never means "not refreshing" or "not blocked". `last_run_status` is unrelated to refresh state: it stays the outcome of the last completed RUN. `auto_refresh_default` is omitted when the notebook has no configured default. `type:"markdown"` marks a prose cell; SQL cells omit `type`. No cell data values; no columns/rows/count. Previews are capped at 120 chars — cells cut carry `preview_truncated: true` + `full_length`; a preview is never a cell's real content to write back.

name: add_cell
description: Append a cell to the notebook. Returns the new cell id and, if run=true, a per-query status array with the same semantics as run_cell (reads run in parallel; an invalid statement is skipped with its error). Writes are never auto-run: a cell containing DDL/DML comes back `{ ran: false, skipped: true }`. You never see query rows or column data. Set type:"markdown" to add a prose cell instead of a SQL cell — its `sql` field then carries the markdown source, it is rendered (never executed), and `run` is ignored.

sql.description: SQL for the cell. May contain multiple statements separated by `;`. In draw mode, multi-statement cells overlay series on a single chart: the first query's timestamp column is the x-axis anchor, subsequent queries contribute additional numeric series merged on the time axis. For a markdown cell (type:"markdown"), this is the markdown source text instead of SQL.

type.description: Cell kind. "markdown" creates a rendered prose cell that is never executed (`run` is ignored). null/omitted = "sql".

after_cell_id.description: Insert after this cell id; pass null to append to the end.

run.description: If true, run the cell immediately after inserting. Response then includes `ran` (true iff every statement succeeded), `queryCount`, and `results: string[]` — one entry per `;`-separated statement, each `"success"`, `"cancelled"`, or `"ERROR: <message>"`. The order matches the cell's SQL. Still no row data. Pass null to skip. Running is DQL-only: a cell containing DDL/DML (INSERT/UPDATE/CREATE/DROP/...) is added but NEVER executed — the response gets `{ ran: false, skipped: true, note: <reason> }`. Markdown cells (type:"markdown") are likewise never executed. Take consent from the user, then call run_cell explicitly.

name: update_cell
description: Replace a cell's value. Overwrites preemptively — cells are auto-saved. Results carry over by content: a statement whose text is unchanged keeps its result and its refresh state, an edited or added one starts empty, and a rewrite that leaves no statement unchanged clears the cell's results. Use to fix a broken SQL cell. When editing part of a long cell, base the new value on a non-truncated read (get_cell with get_full_content: true) — never on a preview or a `truncated: true` read.

name: delete_cell
description: Delete a cell from the notebook.

name: move_cell_up
description: Swap a cell with the one above it.

name: move_cell_down
description: Swap a cell with the one below it.

name: duplicate_cell
description: Duplicate a cell immediately after the original.

name: run_cell
description: Execute a SQL cell. A cell whose statements are all reads runs them in PARALLEL: one failure skips nothing, and a statement the server rejects at validation is skipped with its validation error as that statement's result. A cell containing any DDL/DML runs sequentially instead, and a failure stops the remaining statements. Returns `{ success, queryCount, results: string[] }`, where each `results` entry is `"success"`, `"cancelled"`, or `"ERROR: <message>"`, in source order. You do NOT see columns, rows, or values — call run_query if you need data. `success` is true only when every statement reached `"success"`. This is the ONLY path that executes agent-initiated DDL/DML in a cell (apply_notebook_state and add_cell never auto-run writes) — it requires the 'write' permission and the user's consent. A markdown cell is never executed: the response is `{ ran: false, skipped: true, note: <reason> }`.

name: set_layout_mode
description: Switch a notebook between list and grid layouts.

name: set_cell_layout
description: Position a single cell in grid mode. x/y/w are integers in the react-grid-layout grid; width is limited to 12 columns. Cell height is derived from its semantic pane dimensions. The response includes the applied grid position plus the cell's presented `view` and `mode`; editor-only and markdown cells report mode null, and markdown also reports view null. Use set_cell_dimensions to resize a cell or change its `view`.

name: set_cell_dimensions
description: Resize a cell using semantic pane dimensions in CSS pixels and choose its pane view. Every input field is required by strict tool calling: pass null to preserve the current setting. Pass "auto" for a height to restore automatic sizing, or a number to pin it. For SQL/draw cells, view accepts editor, result, or editor_result. view "editor" is DESTRUCTIVE: it discards the cell's result and snapshot and clears its presented mode — the same gesture as toggling off the table or chart in the UI; the response then carries mode:null and result_discarded:true. The stored result/editor_result arrangement is kept for the next result. A cell with nothing to show reports view "editor" and mode null. Markdown has no pane-view state: it reports `view`, `mode`, and `result_height` as null; editor_height sizes its rendered content, while result_height and view are ignored — keep them null. Use 86px for a polished markdown title. Preset charts need at least 296px; components, custom chart options, and tables need at least 100px. No pane may exceed 2400px.

editor_height.description: Editor pane height in CSS pixels; for markdown, rendered content height. Null preserves, "auto" restores content-driven sizing. SQL editors are at least 72px, markdown at least 56px, and every pane at most 2400px. Use 86px for a polished markdown title.

result_height.description: Result/chart pane height in CSS pixels. Null preserves, "auto" restores result-driven sizing. Maximum 2400px.

view.description: The cell's pane view. Null preserves. result and editor_result store the arrangement. editor DISCARDS the cell's result and snapshot, clears its presented mode, and hides the result pane (the toggle-off gesture); on a cell with nothing to show it is a no-op.

name: set_cell_mode
description: Switch a SQL cell between run (table output) and draw (chart output). Draw cells auto-execute — do not call run_cell afterwards. MULTI-SERIES TIP: a draw-mode cell can hold multiple SELECT statements separated by `;`. The first query's timestamp column is the chart's x-axis (the 'anchor'); every additional query contributes its numeric columns as extra series merged on the time axis. Use this to overlay metrics that come from different tables or different aggregations on a single chart.

name: set_cell_chart_config
description: Configure the chart for a draw-mode cell. The cell's `;`-separated SELECTs AUTO-COMBINE into one chart sharing the first query's x-axis; `queries` holds one config per statement (index-aligned). Queries combine when their x-axis kind matches: all-temporal merge by time, all-categorical merge by category name. Each query keeps its own `type` (line/area/stepLine/stepArea/bar/stackedBar/scatter/pie/candlestick/heatmap/band/rangeBar/boxplot); set `axis:"right"` (+ optional `right_axis`) for a series on a different unit/scale; `enabled:false` opts a query out (the first query is always included — it defines the x-axis). For a candlestick query, supply `ohlc:{open,high,low,close}` (required — a candlestick needs an explicit ohlc mapping). When x_column is a NUMERIC column (not a timestamp/category) it renders as a continuous value axis. Numeric-x charts are single-query (they don't combine). Patch semantics: top-level `x_column`/`right_axis` null = preserve; `queries` null = preserve; `queries: []` clears overrides (back to inference); a non-null `queries` array REPLACES all per-query configs (send one entry per `;`-split statement — a non-empty array whose length differs from the statement count is rejected). pie/scatter/stackedBar only render as a chart of their own (single-query). Type 'events' turns a statement into MARKERS on the time axis (deploys, rollouts, news, incidents): one dashed line per row, or a shaded range when `events.end` is set, labelled from `events.label` and coloured by `events.tone`. Setting `queries` replaces any visual or custom option on the cell (set_cell_visual / set_cell_custom_chart). Column formats (set_cell_formats) format the tooltip and the y-axis. Types heatmap / band / rangeBar / boxplot read the columns in `heatmap` / `band` / `range` / `box` (null = guessed from names and kinds). heatmap, boxplot and a time rangeBar (Gantt) show as a chart of their own; band and a numeric rangeBar combine with other series. Options: `horizontal` lays bar charts down; `percent_stack` stacks area/stackedBar to 100 %; `pie_shape` pie/donut/halfDonut; `scatter.size`/`scatter.color` make a bubble chart; `thresholds` draws the y column's format thresholds as lines or bands.

x_column.description: Shared x-axis column (the first query's). Null preserves.

queries.description: One config per `;`-split query, index-aligned. Send the FULL array — one entry per statement, never a partial subset: a non-null array REPLACES all per-query configs, so any omitted statement loses its config. A non-empty array whose length ≠ the cell's `;`-split statement count is REJECTED. Null (the whole array) preserves the current config; `[]` resets every statement to inference; a `null` entry infers just that statement.

y_columns.description: Columns to plot from THIS query; null = all numeric. Not used for candlestick — set `ohlc` instead.

ohlc.description: Candlestick OHLC mapping. All four required when used; null otherwise.

partition_by_column.description: Categorical column to partition this query's series by; null = none.

axis.description: 'right' = shared secondary axis for a different unit/scale. null = left.

enabled.description: false opts this query out of the chart. null = included. The first query is always included.

tone.description: A column holding tone names (positive, warning, negative, info, accent, muted).

events.description: Only for type 'events': the statement's rows become markers on the time axis instead of a series. time = when (default the first column); end = range end (optional: without it each row is a line); label = text (default the second column).

heatmap.description: Only for type 'heatmap': y = the row column (text or a bucket), value = the column that colours each cell; x is x_column. Null = guessed (first text column, first numeric).

band.description: Only for type 'band': the shaded area between lower and upper (p5/p95, min/max, a forecast range); y_columns draw as lines inside it. Null = guessed from names (low/high, min/max, p5/p95).

range.description: Only for type 'rangeBar': a bar from start to end per x (daily low/high). With TIMESTAMP start and end the chart lies down: one lane per x_column value along a time axis (jobs, windows: a Gantt). Null = guessed (start/end, low/high).

box.description: Only for type 'boxplot': five columns the QUERY computes per x (min, approx_percentile(v, 0.25), approx_percentile(v, 0.5), approx_percentile(v, 0.75), max). Null = guessed from names or the first five numeric columns.

percent_stack.description: Only for area / stepArea / stackedBar: each x's series add up to 100 % (shares of a total, e.g. a generation mix). Null = off.

pie_shape.description: Only for pie: a full pie, a ring (default) or a half ring standing on its flat side (one share of a whole, KPI-like).

scatter.description: Only for scatter: numeric columns that size the points (area grows with the value) and colour them on a light-to-strong scale (bubble chart). Null = plain points.

right_axis.description: Shared right y-axis; meaningful when some query has axis='right'. Null preserves.

horizontal.description: Lay bars down: categories down the side, values across (long labels, rankings). Applies only when every drawn query is bar, stackedBar or a numeric rangeBar. Null preserves; false turns it off.

thresholds.description: Draw the thresholds of the first column drawn on the LEFT axis whose FORMAT has them (set_cell_formats thresholds + base_tone; y columns, band edges and range ends count, percent_stack shares do not): 'lines' = dashed lines with the value, 'bands' = shaded tone bands (ok / warning / breach zones). The axis stretches to show them. Null preserves; 'off' turns it off.

name: set_cell_highlight_config
description: Set or clear the highlight rules of a run-mode cell's result grids (trend coloring): flash cells that moved up or down since the previous refresh, color threshold breaches, band values into steps, or shade a range. One config per cell, applied to every statement's grid by column name; a grid without the column is not affected. Replaces the whole config (PUT). `highlight_config: null` clears it. Typical watchlist: identity_columns ["symbol"], rules [{kind:"previous",column:"price",op:"gt",color:"green"},{kind:"previous",column:"price",op:"lt",color:"red"}]. Pair with set_cell_autorefresh so the grid ticks. Colors are hue names (theme-aware): red, teal, amber, lime, orange, purple, green, pink, blue, olive; red and green are the loss/gain pair.

highlight_config.description: Highlight rules for the cell's result grids. Rules evaluate top-down per cell; the first match colors the background. previous rules also show an up/down glyph.

identity_columns.description: Columns whose values identify the same row across refreshes, e.g. ["symbol","side"]. Needed only by previous rules; may be empty otherwise. A grid missing any of them gets no comparison. Never the designated timestamp for latest-row queries.

kind.description: previous = compare with the same row in the previous result (needs identity_columns). newRow = a row whose identity was not in the previous result (needs identity_columns); it always paints the whole row and takes only color and display, so send column null. value = compare with a fixed value; op between with fill gradient shades by position in the range. steps = ascending thresholds, one color each, value >= from, highest wins; base_color below the first.

column.description: Result column the rule targets. null = every numeric column (ignored by newRow).

enabled.description: false keeps the rule but skips it. null = enabled.

display.description: UI labels: Flash = temporary (briefly highlight matching cells, then fade out); Permanent = always (keep matching cells highlighted until the next result). Use these UI labels when describing the display mode to the user, but send temporary or always in this field. null = temporary for previous rules, always otherwise.

applies_to.description: What a match colors: cell = only the matching cell, row = every cell of the row. null = cell. List order decides per cell; a row rule listed first paints the whole row, a cell rule listed first keeps its cell.

color.description: Cell color for previous and value rules; for between with fill gradient, the color at the `value` end. null = teal. Use green/red for up/down (the gain/loss pair).

op.description: previous: gt|lt|changed|changedBy. value: gt|gte|lt|lte|eq|between|isNull|contains|matches. null for steps and newRow. Per column type: numeric takes everything except contains/matches; timestamp takes gt/lt/changed, the ordering ops, eq, between (solid fill) and isNull; text takes changed, eq, isNull, contains and matches; boolean takes changed, eq and isNull; other types (arrays, uuid, …) take changed and isNull. A condition that does not fit the column never matches.

value.description: value rules: the comparison value (gt/gte/lt/lte/eq), or the lower bound for between. Plain value, no quotes; a number with more than 15 significant digits (a LONG id past 2^53, a high-scale DECIMAL) as a string, so JSON keeps every digit. Timestamps as ISO strings only (YYYY-MM-DD[THH:mm[:ss[.fraction]]], up to 9 fraction digits), read as UTC unless they carry a zone; other date forms are rejected. For between, null = auto: the column's current minimum, recomputed on every result.

to.description: value between: the upper bound, inclusive; a number with more than 15 significant digits as a string. null = auto: the column's current maximum, recomputed on every result.

threshold.description: previous changedBy: minimum change to match, inclusive (|change| >= threshold), 0 or more; 0 = any change, unchanged cells never match.

unit.description: previous changedBy: threshold unit. null = percent.

text.description: value contains: case-insensitive substring (eq on text ignores case too). value matches: an RE2 regular expression (linear time; no backreferences or lookarounds), e.g. ^EUR; there are no /…/flags, put (?i) in front to ignore case, e.g. (?i)eur.

steps.description: steps: thresholds; a value takes the highest step it reaches (value >= from). Below the lowest step it takes base_color.

base_color.description: steps: color for values below the lowest step. null = amber.

fill.description: value between only. solid = one color inside the range (default). gradient = shade from `color` at `value` to `high_color` at `to`, mixed in between and clamped beyond the ends; matches every numeric cell. With value and to both null the scale always spans the column's current min and max.

high_color.description: value between with fill gradient: the color at the `to` end. null = green.

name: get_cell_image
description: A PNG picture of a draw cell's chart as the console shows it now (theme, size, layout, data), with the cell's render_report. Use it to check how a chart LOOKS after set_cell_chart_config / set_cell_visual / set_cell_custom_chart / define_chart_type: overlapping or cut labels, empty space, unreadable colours, a chart that draws nothing. The notebook must be open in the console (activate_notebook); a cell off screen is scrolled into view first. Components drawn in HTML (stat, bullet, orderBook, uptime, planTree) have no picture: the result says so and carries their render_report. If another cell is maximized, only that one is drawn: clear it with set_cell_maximized first. Needs the 'read' permission (the picture shows query results). Returns {picture, width, height, render_report} plus the image.

name: set_cell_visual
description:
Draw a draw-mode cell as a COMPONENT instead of a chart: stat tiles, gauge, bullet, order book, state timeline, treemap, sunburst, graph, Sankey, chord, map, liquidity heatmap, volume profile or query plan tree. The console styles it; the QUERY does the shaping (aggregation, bucketing, sorting) and the component maps as little as possible. Roles map columns by name; every role has a default, so a query that returns the documented column order needs no mapping. The cell must be in draw mode (set_cell_mode 'draw'). Column formats (set_cell_formats) set number formats and colour thresholds; set_cell_interactions makes clicks set a variable. visual:null removes the visual (back to the preset chart). After it draws, get_cell returns render_report with what was drawn and any missing columns.

TYPES (statements are the cell's ;-separated SELECTs, first = statement 0):
- stat: one tile per row of statement 0. value (default: first numeric), label (default: first text column), caption (optional text under the value, e.g. '254 use WAL'), change (a FRACTION, e.g. 0.012 = +1.2%; default: a column named change). Sparkline: statement `sparkline_query` (default statement 1) with rows (time, value[, label]); rows whose label matches the tile's draw its line. Tip: SELECT symbol, last(price) price, last(price)/first(price)-1 change FROM t WHERE ts > dateadd('d',-1,now()); SELECT ts, symbol, last(price) price FROM t SAMPLE BY 5m.
- gauge: first row of statement 0. value, label; min/max (default 0..100, or 0..1 when the value's format is percent); colour bands from the value column's format thresholds.
- bullet: one bar per row: label, value, target (default: a column named target, limit, budget or max); min/max; bands from thresholds. For limit usage, VaR vs limit.
- orderBook: statement 0 = ASKS, best (lowest price) first; statement 1 = BIDS, best (highest price) first. price and size = first two columns (or columns.price/size); a third column shows as is (cumulative size, order count). Spread and mid are shown; depth bars update without flashing. Use formats for price decimals (kind price) and size (compact).
- stateTimeline: coloured state bands per lane. time (default: first timestamp), lane (default: first text), state; end optional (default: the lane's next row). States named ok/up/active colour positive, down/error/failed negative, warning/degraded warning; `severity` overrides.
- uptime: a status page. Same rows as stateTimeline (time, lane, state[, end]); per lane the current state, `buckets` bars over the time range each coloured by the worst state inside it (hover lists the time per state), and the uptime %. For service, replication or device health.
- treemap / sunburst: path = text columns from outer to inner level (default: all text columns in order), value (default: first numeric) sizes the leaf; change (optional, a number) colours leaves on a red-to-green diverging scale (market movers).
- graph / sankey / chord: from, to, value (default: columns 1, 2, 3). graph = force layout sized by flow; sankey = flows left to right; chord = flows around a circle.
- map: world map. Either region (country name as in Natural Earth, e.g. 'Germany', 'United States of America') + value, coloured on a scale; or lat + lon (+ value, label) as sized points.
- liquidityHeatmap: time x price cells coloured by value (time, price, value; default first timestamp, first and second numerics). Bucket in SQL (SAMPLE BY, round(price, n)). Optional statement 1 (time, price) draws a price line on top.
- volumeProfile: horizontal volume per price level: price, buy, sell (default columns 1-3) or value; marks the point of control.
- planTree: statement 0 is EXPLAIN <query>; draws the plan as an operator tree with attributes.

columns.description: Column roles, by column name. Null = the default (by position or kind, see the tool description).

sparkline_query.description: stat: 0-based index of the statement whose rows (time, value[, label]) draw each tile's sparkline. Null = the second statement when there is one.

animate_digits.description: Stat tiles and order book: roll changed digits in the main value or mid price. Null or false is off.

buckets.description: uptime: bars the time range splits into (e.g. 90 for 90 days of daily rows). Fewer are drawn when the panel is narrow. Null = 90.

severity.description: stateTimeline / uptime: what a state means when its name does not say (e.g. {state:'charging', level:'warning'}). Uptime = time not in a bad state. Null = by name.

name: set_cell_custom_chart
description:
Draw a draw-mode cell from an ECharts option you write as JSON (option_json, a JSON string), for charts no preset or visual covers: radar, polar bars, funnel, boxplot, parallel, themeRiver, calendar heatmap, pictorialBar, matrix, broken axes, custom series, combinations. option_json:null removes it (back to the preset chart). The cell must be in draw mode.

DATA: never put rows in the option. Each statement of the cell is a dataset with id "q0", "q1", … whose dimensions are the column names; series bind with {"datasetId":"q0","encode":{"x":"ts","y":"price"}} (timestamps become a time axis). For series that do not read datasets (graph, sankey, chord, tree, treemap, sunburst, gauge, radar, funnel, heatmap tuples, axis category lists), put a placeholder where the data goes: {"$rows":{"query":0,"shape":S,…}} with shape: tuples (columns:[…]) → [[a,b,c],…]; column (column) → [v,…]; value (column) → first row's number; items (name, value or [values]) → [{name,value}]; tree (path:[…], value, color) → nested children; links (source,target,value) → [{source,target,value}]; nodes (source,target) → [{name}]; lines (columns:[from lon, from lat, to lon, to lat], name, value) → [{coords,name,value}] for a lines series on geo. You may add your own datasets with transforms ({"fromDatasetId":"q0","transform":{"type":"filter",…}}) using other ids.

LAYOUT: the console lays the chart out for the panel; do not tune paddings. Grid, calendar, geo, parallel, singleAxis, matrix and the boxes of funnel/sankey/tree/treemap/graph/map, and the center/radius of pie/gauge/sunburst/chord/radar/polar, are fitted to the panel with room for their labels; only their ARRANGEMENT is kept (two grids stacked 70/30, concentric rings, a pie beside a grid). Legends, shown visualMaps and zoom sliders always sit along the bottom. A title placed inside the chart (top: '45%') is an overlay that moves with the chart (e.g. a total in a donut's middle); a title at the edge gets its own band, but the cell name is already the heading.

STYLE: the console theme sets fonts, palette, axes, tooltips and background; fonts and literal colours are REMOVED. Colour with tones: "$positive", "$negative", "$warning", "$info", "$accent", "$neutral", "$muted", "$series1"…"$series8", optionally with opacity "$positive:0.3" (anywhere a colour goes, including visualMap inRange.color and gradient colorStops).

NO JAVASCRIPT: functions cannot be expressed. Formatters are string templates ({a} series, {b} name, {c} value, {d} percent, label templates also {@column}); HTML in tooltip templates is shown as text. Title links, tooltip DOM options and the toolbox are removed; images must be data: URIs. custom series name a renderItem: built-in barRange, lineRange, stage, violin, contour, segmentedDoughnut, or a notebook chart type from define_chart_type. Maps: "world" (geo or map series; country names as in Natural Earth).

The response lists problems found now (removed colours, unknown series types); get_cell's render_report adds problems found while drawing (e.g. encode columns missing from a dataset). Example: {"radar":{"indicator":{"$rows":{"query":0,"shape":"items","name":"metric","value":"max"}}},"series":[{"type":"radar","data":[{"name":"today","value":{"$rows":{"query":0,"shape":"column","column":"value"}},"areaStyle":{"color":"$series2:0.25"}}]}]}

option_json.description: The ECharts option as a JSON string, or null to remove it.

name: set_cell_formats
description: Set how a cell's columns read, by column name, everywhere the cell shows them: result grid text, colours and in-cell bars/meters/sparklines; preset chart tooltips and y-axis labels; stat tiles, gauges, bullets, the order book and other visuals. Also sets the grid's live mode. formats: a non-null array REPLACES all formats ([] clears them); null keeps them. grid_mode: 'stable' keeps each row in place across refreshes (by the highlight identity columns; for watchlists sorted by a moving value), 'stream' flashes rows that are new since the last refresh (trade tapes, logs; order the query newest first and LIMIT it), 'default' clears; null keeps it.

kind.description: number: grouped digits. percent: the value is a FRACTION (0.05 shows 5%). price: fixed decimals. bytes: KB/MB/GB. duration: the value is MILLISECONDS. text: as returned.

suffix.description: A unit, e.g. " ms" or " USD". Max 16 characters.

thresholds.description: Ascending: a value at or above `value` takes `tone`. Colours grid text, stat values, gauge and bullet bands.

visual.description: Result grid only: bar = scaled to the column's range (signed values grow from zero); meter = share of the column total; sparkline = draws an ARRAY column's values (e.g. array_agg(price)); on other columns it draws nothing.

name: set_cell_interactions
description: Make a cell's result drive notebook variables (cross-filtering): click sets a variable from the clicked item, brush sets two variables from a dragged time window. Cells whose SQL uses @variable refresh right away. Full replace: both null removes the interactions. Works on preset charts, visuals, custom charts and run-mode grids (click only). Variables a click creates start empty; declare them with a default in apply_notebook_state `variables` so dependent cells have a value before the first click.

column.description: Column whose value the click sets. Null = the clicked item's name (category, slice, node, tile label) or, in a grid, the clicked cell.

click.description: A click on a bar, slice, point, node, tile, order book level or grid row sets @variable to the clicked value (as a SQL literal: text quoted, numbers as they are). Cells that use the variable refresh.

brush.description: Dragging across a time chart (preset or custom, time x-axis) sets the two variables to the window's bounds as quoted ISO timestamps, e.g. '2026-01-01T10:02:00.000Z'. Use them as WHERE ts BETWEEN @from AND @to.

name: define_chart_type
description: Define (or replace) a notebook chart type: an ECharts custom-series renderItem written as JavaScript, usable by name from any custom chart option in this notebook ({"type":"custom","renderItem":"<name>","datasetId":"q0","encode":{…}}). Draw INSIDE the plot: the console fits the plot area to the panel and only knows about axis labels, so marks or text a renderItem draws past api.coord of the axis range overflow the panel. Leave room in data space instead (e.g. xAxis max 120 for a 0-100 bar with its value written after it). Use it for marks no built-in series draws (lanes, ranges, glyphs, annotated boxes). render_item is a function expression `function (params, api) { … }` or a function body using params and api. It is called once per data item and returns a graphic element or null, e.g. {type:'rect', shape:{x,y,width,height}, style:{fill: api.visual('color')}}. Useful api: api.value(dim) (dimension index or column name), api.coord([x, y]) → pixel point, api.size([dx, dy]) → pixel size of a data step, api.visual('color'); params.coordSys has x, y, width, height of the plot; params.itemPayload is the series' itemPayload object. Return group elements ({type:'group', children:[…]}) for several shapes. Colours: take them from api.visual('color') or the series itemStyle (where tones like "$accent" work), not literals. Errors thrown while drawing show in get_cell's render_report. EXPERIMENTAL: the function runs in the console page with the user's rights, so it runs only when allowed: types defined with the 'write' permission are allowed; otherwise (and for imported notebooks) the user allows them in the notebook's Chart types dialog, and charts using them show that they wait. get_chart_type and get_notebook_state report `allowed`.

name.description: Letters, digits, _; starts with a letter; max 64.

name: get_chart_type
description: Read a notebook chart type's renderItem source and description, `allowed` (false: its code does not run until the user allows it), and `used_by`: the ids of the cells whose custom option draws with it (names are listed in get_notebook_state chart_types). People edit, rename and delete chart types in the notebook toolbar's Chart types dialog; a rename there renames the uses too.

name: delete_chart_type
description: Delete a notebook chart type. Custom options that still use it stop drawing those series; the result's note names those cells.

name: set_notebook_chart_sync
description: Link the notebook's time charts (a notebook editor setting): crosshair 'line' shows the hovered time on every other time chart, 'tooltip' also opens their tooltips, 'off' none; zoom true zooms every time chart to the same window when one is zoomed.

name: set_cell_autorefresh
description: Set auto-refresh polling for a cell, as a per-cell override of the notebook default (set_notebook_autorefresh). Applies to both chart (draw-mode) and grid (run-mode) cells. A cell containing DDL/DML never polls: the value is stored, but the engine blocks its ticks and read tools report `auto_refresh_blocked: "contains_write"`. Markdown cells are rejected. Nothing polls without a per-cell value or a notebook default. `value`: true = adaptive poll (interval auto-tuned to response time), false = no polling, a fixed interval string (digits plus ms, s or m, from 50ms to 60m, e.g. "250ms", "5s", "15m"), or null to clear the override so the cell inherits the notebook default.

anyOf.description: Fixed interval: digits plus ms, s or m, from 50ms to 60m, e.g. "250ms", "5s", "15m".

name: set_notebook_autorefresh
description: Set the notebook-level auto-refresh default for every cell showing a chart or a grid. Cells with no per-cell value inherit it; set_cell_autorefresh sets a per-cell override that wins over it. Cells containing DDL/DML are skipped — auto-refresh never executes a write. Until this is set, nothing polls. `value`: true = adaptive poll (interval auto-tuned to response time), false = no polling, or a fixed interval string (digits plus ms, s or m, from 50ms to 60m, e.g. "250ms", "5s", "15m"). `reset_cell_overrides: true` additionally deletes every per-cell override in the same atomic call, so ALL cells follow the new default — the equivalent of the console's "Reset cell overrides" action. Nothing re-runs; false or null leaves per-cell overrides in place and they keep winning over the default.

anyOf.description: Fixed interval: digits plus ms, s or m, from 50ms to 60m, e.g. "250ms", "5s", "15m".

name: set_cell_name
description: Set or clear a cell's name (its display label in the cell header). Applies to any cell; for a chart cell it is also the chart title. Pass null to clear.

name.description: Cell name (max 100 characters). Pass null to clear.

name: apply_notebook_state
description: Bulk-apply the entire desired state of a notebook in one atomic call. Use this for bulk edits spanning multiple cells or creating a notebook from scratch. Use update_cell or set_cell_* for small operations. Use INSTEAD OF chained add_cell + update_cell + set_cell_mode + set_cell_chart_config only when composing a multi-cell layout from scratch, changing many cells at once, or restructuring an existing notebook. The cells array is the COMPLETE desired list: cells in the current notebook whose id is missing from your request are DELETED. For new cells, omit `id` and one will be generated. Each cell carries exactly one of `value` (full verbatim SQL) or `preserve_value: true` (keep the existing cell's SQL, results, and run history unchanged). A changed `value` carries results over by content: a statement whose text is unchanged keeps its result, an edited or added one starts empty, and a rewrite that leaves nothing unchanged clears the cell's results — prefer preserve_value for every cell whose SQL you are not changing, and NEVER send a value reconstructed from a preview or a truncated get_cell read. Charts in mode='draw' render automatically — do not call run_cell afterwards. Cells with resolved mode='run' (explicit, or omitted: new defaults to 'run', existing preserves) auto-execute after the apply — EXCEPT cells whose statements include DDL/DML (INSERT/UPDATE/CREATE/DROP/...): those are NEVER auto-executed (their `runs` entry gets `skipped: true`), so applying state can never trigger a write's side effects. Take consent from the user, then call run_cell explicitly to execute them. Markdown cells (type:"markdown") are rendered prose and are likewise never auto-run. Auto-executed read-only cells run their statements in PARALLEL (one failure skips nothing; a statement rejected at validation is skipped with its validation error). Each cell also accepts `auto_refresh` — the same per-cell override set_cell_autorefresh writes. The response includes a `runs: [{cellId, success, queryCount?, results?, error?, skipped?}]` array — `results` is the per-statement status list (`"success"` / `"cancelled"` / `"ERROR: <message>"`); a top-level `error` is set only when the run was refused before any statement executed. The response also carries `results_cleared`: the ids of cells whose whole result this apply discarded (view:"editor", or a changed value that kept no statement unchanged); it is empty when nothing was cleared, and a cell that keeps some statement results is not listed. Always call get_workspace_state first; the state-freshness gate applies. Dashboard fields: chart_config.visual / chart_config.custom_option_json draw a component or a custom ECharts option (a draw cell with one of them may send queries:[]); formats, interactions and grid_mode are per cell (PUT, like highlight_config); chart_types and chart_sync are notebook-wide (null keeps them).

layout_mode.description: Notebook layout mode after this apply. Null preserves current.

anyOf.description: Fixed interval: digits plus ms, s or m, from 50ms to 60m, e.g. "250ms", "5s", "15m".

auto_refresh_default.description: Notebook-level auto-refresh default after this apply. Cells with no per-cell auto_refresh inherit it. Null preserves current.

maximized_cell_id.description: Spotlight one cell id, or null to clear. Pass null to clear.

variables.description: Ordered notebook-scoped global variables to be referenced as @var in the query (the DECLARE block surfaced in the Variables popover). Each item is {"name": "from", "value": "dateadd('d', -7, now())"}; names have no leading '@'. Order matters: if one variable references another, place the dependency first and the dependent variable later. Values are sent as a notebook-scoped `DECLARE` block prepended to each cell statement (or merged into the cell's own `DECLARE` block when present). Globals are server-resolved at parse time, so operator precedence and lexical shadowing follow QuestDB's `DECLARE` semantics. For non-`SELECT` statement forms (`INSERT`/`CREATE`/`UPDATE`/`ALTER`/…) globals are not injected; declare locally inside the inner `SELECT` if needed. Pass null to preserve current; pass [] to clear all.

cells.description: Complete desired cell list, in order. Cell at index N gets position N. Missing existing-cell ids are deleted.

id.description: Existing cell id to update, or null/omitted for a new cell.

name.description: Cell name (its header label; for a chart cell it is also the chart title; max 100 characters). apply is a full PUT — a string sets it, null/"" clears it (the existing name is NOT preserved). Read the current name from the cell in <notebook_context> / get_notebook_state.

value.description: SQL text of the cell, VERBATIM and COMPLETE (from a non-truncated get_cell read; never from a preview or a `truncated: true` read). May contain multiple statements separated by `;`. In draw mode, this overlays series on one chart: the first query's timestamp is the x-axis anchor; subsequent queries contribute extra numeric series merged on time. Use this to combine metrics from different tables or different aggregations into a single chart. Null/omitted REQUIRES preserve_value: true.

preserve_value.description: True keeps the existing cell's current SQL unchanged (and with it the cell's results and run history) instead of echoing it — exactly one of value / preserve_value:true per cell. PREFER this for every cell whose SQL you are not changing; it is the only safe option when your copy may be stale (STATE_STALE retry) or came from a truncated read. Existing-id cells only.

type.description: Cell kind. "markdown" makes this a rendered prose cell — `value` is markdown source, and `mode`/`chart_config` MUST be null (rejected otherwise). It is never executed or auto-run. Cell kind is FIXED for the life of a cell: null/omitted preserves an existing cell's kind, and sending the other kind for an existing id is rejected — delete the cell and add a new one instead. New cells default to "sql".

mode.description: Requested result mode. Null defaults to 'run' for new cells and preserves the current mode for existing cells, except that view='editor' is authoritative and clears the presented mode. An explicit 'run' or 'draw' cannot be combined with view='editor'.

anyOf.description: Fixed interval: digits plus ms, s or m, from 50ms to 60m, e.g. "250ms", "5s", "15m".

auto_refresh.description: Per-cell auto-refresh value: true = adaptive poll, false = off, or a fixed interval string (digits plus ms, s or m, from 50ms to 60m, e.g. "250ms", "5s", "15m"). Omitted or null stores NO override — the cell inherits the notebook's auto_refresh_default.

editor_height.description: Editor pane height in CSS pixels; for markdown, rendered content height. Null preserves an existing setting (default auto for a new cell); "auto" restores content-driven sizing. SQL editors are at least 72px, markdown at least 56px, and every pane at most 2400px. Use 86px for a polished markdown title.

result_height.description: Result/chart pane height in CSS pixels. Null preserves an existing setting (default auto for a new cell); "auto" restores result-driven sizing. Preset charts need at least 296px; components, custom chart options, and tables need at least 100px. Maximum 2400px. Ignored for markdown; keep it null.

view.description: The cell's pane view. Null preserves an existing setting. result and editor_result store the arrangement. editor is authoritative: it DISCARDS an existing cell's result and snapshot, clears its presented mode, and hides the result pane (the toggle-off gesture; the cell is then listed in results_cleared). Send mode:null with view:'editor'; an explicit mode 'run' or 'draw' is rejected as contradictory. New draw cells default to result; other new SQL cells default to editor_result but report editor with mode null until a result exists. Ignored for markdown; keep it null.

chart_config.description: Chart configuration; required when mode='draw'. apply_notebook_state is a full PUT — this REPLACES the cell's chart entirely; null/omitted means NO chart (it is NOT preserved). To keep an existing chart unchanged, re-send its full config (shown as `chart_config` on the cell in <notebook_context> / get_notebook_state). The cell's `;`-separated SELECTs auto-combine into one chart sharing the first query's x-axis; `queries` holds one config per statement (each keeps its own type; axis:'right' for a second scale).

queries.description: One config per `;`-split query, index-aligned — send the FULL array, exactly one entry per statement (its length must equal the cell's `;`-split statement count, else REJECTED). These entries are the chart's per-query configs in full (apply is a PUT); a `null` entry infers that statement. To keep a chart unchanged, re-send its full config from <notebook_context>.

tone.description: A column holding tone names (positive, warning, negative, info, accent, muted).

events.description: Only for type 'events': the statement's rows become markers on the time axis instead of a series. time = when (default the first column); end = range end (optional: without it each row is a line); label = text (default the second column).

heatmap.description: Only for type 'heatmap': y = the row column (text or a bucket), value = the column that colours each cell; x is x_column. Null = guessed (first text column, first numeric).

band.description: Only for type 'band': the shaded area between lower and upper (p5/p95, min/max, a forecast range); y_columns draw as lines inside it. Null = guessed from names (low/high, min/max, p5/p95).

range.description: Only for type 'rangeBar': a bar from start to end per x (daily low/high). With TIMESTAMP start and end the chart lies down: one lane per x_column value along a time axis (jobs, windows: a Gantt). Null = guessed (start/end, low/high).

box.description: Only for type 'boxplot': five columns the QUERY computes per x (min, approx_percentile(v, 0.25), approx_percentile(v, 0.5), approx_percentile(v, 0.75), max). Null = guessed from names or the first five numeric columns.

percent_stack.description: Only for area / stepArea / stackedBar: each x's series add up to 100 % (shares of a total, e.g. a generation mix). Null = off.

pie_shape.description: Only for pie: a full pie, a ring (default) or a half ring standing on its flat side (one share of a whole, KPI-like).

scatter.description: Only for scatter: numeric columns that size the points (area grows with the value) and colour them on a light-to-strong scale (bubble chart). Null = plain points.

columns.description: Column roles, by column name. Null = the default (by position or kind, see the tool description).

sparkline_query.description: stat: 0-based index of the statement whose rows (time, value[, label]) draw each tile's sparkline. Null = the second statement when there is one.

animate_digits.description: Stat tiles and order book: roll changed digits in the main value or mid price. Null or false is off.

buckets.description: uptime: bars the time range splits into (e.g. 90 for 90 days of daily rows). Fewer are drawn when the panel is narrow. Null = 90.

severity.description: stateTimeline / uptime: what a state means when its name does not say (e.g. {state:'charging', level:'warning'}). Uptime = time not in a bad state. Null = by name.

custom_option_json.description: A custom ECharts option as JSON (see set_cell_custom_chart).

horizontal.description: Lay bars down: categories down the side, values across (long labels, rankings). Applies only when every drawn query is bar, stackedBar or a numeric rangeBar. Null = off.

thresholds.description: Draw the thresholds of the first column drawn on the LEFT axis whose FORMAT has them (set_cell_formats thresholds + base_tone; y columns, band edges and range ends count, percent_stack shares do not): 'lines' = dashed lines with the value, 'bands' = shaded tone bands (ok / warning / breach zones). The axis stretches to show them. Null = off.

highlight_config.description: Highlight rules for the cell's result grids, applied to every statement's grid by column name. Omitting clears the cell's rules (full PUT) — copy the current `highlight_config` from <notebook_context> to keep them.

identity_columns.description: Columns whose values identify the same row across refreshes, e.g. ["symbol","side"]. Needed only by previous rules; may be empty otherwise. A grid missing any of them gets no comparison. Never the designated timestamp for latest-row queries.

kind.description: previous = compare with the same row in the previous result (needs identity_columns). newRow = a row whose identity was not in the previous result (needs identity_columns); it always paints the whole row and takes only color and display, so send column null. value = compare with a fixed value; op between with fill gradient shades by position in the range. steps = ascending thresholds, one color each, value >= from, highest wins; base_color below the first.

column.description: Result column the rule targets. null = every numeric column (ignored by newRow).

enabled.description: false keeps the rule but skips it. null = enabled.

display.description: UI labels: Flash = temporary (briefly highlight matching cells, then fade out); Permanent = always (keep matching cells highlighted until the next result). Use these UI labels when describing the display mode to the user, but send temporary or always in this field. null = temporary for previous rules, always otherwise.

applies_to.description: What a match colors: cell = only the matching cell, row = every cell of the row. null = cell. List order decides per cell; a row rule listed first paints the whole row, a cell rule listed first keeps its cell.

color.description: Cell color for previous and value rules; for between with fill gradient, the color at the `value` end. null = teal. Use green/red for up/down (the gain/loss pair).

op.description: previous: gt|lt|changed|changedBy. value: gt|gte|lt|lte|eq|between|isNull|contains|matches. null for steps and newRow. Per column type: numeric takes everything except contains/matches; timestamp takes gt/lt/changed, the ordering ops, eq, between (solid fill) and isNull; text takes changed, eq, isNull, contains and matches; boolean takes changed, eq and isNull; other types (arrays, uuid, …) take changed and isNull. A condition that does not fit the column never matches.

value.description: value rules: the comparison value (gt/gte/lt/lte/eq), or the lower bound for between. Plain value, no quotes; a number with more than 15 significant digits (a LONG id past 2^53, a high-scale DECIMAL) as a string, so JSON keeps every digit. Timestamps as ISO strings only (YYYY-MM-DD[THH:mm[:ss[.fraction]]], up to 9 fraction digits), read as UTC unless they carry a zone; other date forms are rejected. For between, null = auto: the column's current minimum, recomputed on every result.

to.description: value between: the upper bound, inclusive; a number with more than 15 significant digits as a string. null = auto: the column's current maximum, recomputed on every result.

threshold.description: previous changedBy: minimum change to match, inclusive (|change| >= threshold), 0 or more; 0 = any change, unchanged cells never match.

unit.description: previous changedBy: threshold unit. null = percent.

text.description: value contains: case-insensitive substring (eq on text ignores case too). value matches: an RE2 regular expression (linear time; no backreferences or lookarounds), e.g. ^EUR; there are no /…/flags, put (?i) in front to ignore case, e.g. (?i)eur.

steps.description: steps: thresholds; a value takes the highest step it reaches (value >= from). Below the lowest step it takes base_color.

base_color.description: steps: color for values below the lowest step. null = amber.

fill.description: value between only. solid = one color inside the range (default). gradient = shade from `color` at `value` to `high_color` at `to`, mixed in between and clamped beyond the ends; matches every numeric cell. With value and to both null the scale always spans the column's current min and max.

high_color.description: value between with fill gradient: the color at the `to` end. null = green.

grid.description: Grid position when layout_mode='grid'. The 12 columns apply to width only (w ≤ 12); height is derived from editor_height, result_height, and view.

kind.description: number: grouped digits. percent: the value is a FRACTION (0.05 shows 5%). price: fixed decimals. bytes: KB/MB/GB. duration: the value is MILLISECONDS. text: as returned.

suffix.description: A unit, e.g. " ms" or " USD". Max 16 characters.

thresholds.description: Ascending: a value at or above `value` takes `tone`. Colours grid text, stat values, gauge and bullet bands.

visual.description: Result grid only: bar = scaled to the column's range (signed values grow from zero); meter = share of the column total; sparkline = draws an ARRAY column's values (e.g. array_agg(price)); on other columns it draws nothing.

formats.description: Column formats (see set_cell_formats). PUT: null/omitted clears them.

column.description: Column whose value the click sets. Null = the clicked item's name (category, slice, node, tile label) or, in a grid, the clicked cell.

click.description: A click on a bar, slice, point, node, tile, order book level or grid row sets @variable to the clicked value (as a SQL literal: text quoted, numbers as they are). Cells that use the variable refresh.

brush.description: Dragging across a time chart (preset or custom, time x-axis) sets the two variables to the window's bounds as quoted ISO timestamps, e.g. '2026-01-01T10:02:00.000Z'. Use them as WHERE ts BETWEEN @from AND @to.

interactions.description: Click and drag interactions (see set_cell_interactions). PUT: null clears them.

grid_mode.description: Grid live mode (see set_cell_formats). PUT: null clears it.

chart_types.description: Notebook chart types (see define_chart_type). Null keeps the current ones; an array replaces them all. A type keeps the user's allowance when its code is unchanged; new or changed code runs only with the 'write' permission, else after the user allows it (get_notebook_state shows `allowed`).

chart_sync.description: Linked time charts (see set_notebook_chart_sync). Null keeps the current setting.

name: set_cell_maximized
description: Spotlight one cell (or null to restore normal layout). Hides other cells in the notebook view.

cell_id.description: Cell id to spotlight, or null to clear.

name: run_query
description: Execute an arbitrary SQL statement against the user's QuestDB instance and return the result rows so you can inspect data, validate work, or compose follow-up queries. UNLIKE `run_cell`, this tool DOES return data values. Default limit is 100 rows; pass `limit` (max 10000) to request more. The response payload is capped at ~1 MB — rows beyond that are dropped from the tail. The response includes `truncated`, `total_count`, and `returned_count` so you know exactly what was clipped. DDL/DML (CREATE / INSERT / UPDATE / DROP / etc.) is allowed and executes against the live database — be deliberate. Auth + connection are handled by the user's already-authenticated browser session.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return (default 100, max 10000). Pass null for default.

name: get_workspace_state
description:
If notebook tools fail with BRIDGE_NOT_PAIRED, call get_pairing_credentials to begin pairing (the response includes a one-click URL to show the user; authentication runs in the browser, the bridge never sees credentials). Once paired, call get_workspace_state at the start of every notebook turn; the digest of edits since your last fetch is in get_recent_user_actions.

Return the current workspace + notebook context as text. Use this at the start of every notebook turn so you know which notebook is active, what cells exist, layout mode, chart configs, and last-run statuses. SQL/draw cells report their pane `view`: "editor" while there is nothing to show, else the stored result or editor_result arrangement. Their `mode` matches that presentation: null for editor-only, `run` for a table result, and `draw` for a chart. Markdown reports `view`, `mode`, and `result_height` as null. Pass include_user_events=true to also receive the digest of edits the user made since your last fetch.

name: get_recent_user_actions
description:
If notebook tools fail with BRIDGE_NOT_PAIRED, call get_pairing_credentials to begin pairing (the response includes a one-click URL to show the user; authentication runs in the browser, the bridge never sees credentials). Once paired, call get_workspace_state at the start of every notebook turn; the digest of edits since your last fetch is in get_recent_user_actions.

Return the digest of user edits to the notebook since your last fetch (or session start). Use this to detect that the user changed something the agent might want to react to. Coalesced — multiple typing events on the same cell collapse to a single 'edited' entry.
